Why These Roles? EHDS Regulatory Backgro: Why These Roles? EHDS Regulatory Background
The European Health Data Space regulatio: The European Health Data Space regulation establishes a governance framework for both primary use (patient access to their own data) and secondary use (research, innovation, policy-making). Each role in this platform maps to a specific actor defined in the regulation:
Healthcare providers, insurers, and regi: Healthcare providers, insurers, and registries that hold electronic health data are legally required to make it available for authorized secondary use. They retain sovereignty over their data and control access through ODRL policies and contract negotiation.
Researchers, public health agencies, and: Researchers, public health agencies, and innovators who need health data for permitted purposes must apply through an HDAB, receive a data permit, and access data only in a secure processing environment. They never receive raw patient data directly.
Each EU Member State must designate one: Each EU Member State must designate one or more Health Data Access Bodies (HDABs) as the national authority that reviews data access applications, issues data permits, and ensures compliance. MedReg DE represents the German HDAB in this implementation.
The dataspace operator runs the technica: The dataspace operator runs the technical infrastructure: participant onboarding, connector management, federated catalog, and transfer monitoring. They ensure interoperability across all participants but do not access health data directly.
The EHDS mandates pseudonymisation and r: The EHDS mandates pseudonymisation and re-identification controls. The Trust Center manages pseudonym resolution, secure processing environment (SPE) sessions, and ensures that data users only access de-identified data. This role enforces the technical privacy safeguards the regulation requires.

A researcher with a data permit asks a q: A researcher with a data permit asks a question in plain language. A prepared question, a fulltext search or, where one is configured, a language model turns it into Cypher, which runs inside the secure processing environment; the page shows the Cypher, the permit it ran under and the rows that came back. The Federated button asks every SPE and merges the answers. Every answer about persons is k-anonymous: a count below 5 is shown as <5, and a share computed from it with it.
Example: A researcher asks “What is the: Example: A researcher asks “What is the age distribution?”; the 0-17 group holds one person and comes back as <5, with a k = 5 badge saying how many values were suppressed.
Row-level data is processed only inside: Row-level data is processed only inside a secure processing environment (EHDS Art. 73); only answers leave it. SPE-1 holds AlphaKlinik Berlin's patients, SPE-2 Limburg Medical Centre's, each a Neo4j workspace loaded for the permit, so a federated question has two contributors. Both apply the same rules before anything leaves: the data permit, the ODRL policy, the Art. 71 opt-out (persons who opted out are never counted) and k = 5, including the rule that a contributor with fewer than 5 records withholds the whole answer, since a missing contributor would identify people. Every question is recorded on the audit chain.

The governance modules manage EHDS compl: The governance modules manage EHDS compliance, protocol testing, and verifiable credential issuance as required by the European Health Data Space regulation (Chapter IV, Art. 50 to 81). These modules ensure that every data access follows the legally mandated approval chain: application, HDAB review, data permit issuance, contract negotiation, and audited transfer.
Manage data access permits as required b: Manage data access permits as required by EHDS Art. 67 and 68. Data users submit applications specifying the purpose, scope, and duration of data access. HDABs review applications against the permitted purposes in Art. 53(1) and issue verifiable credentials as proof of authorization.
Example: PharmaCo Research AG submits a: Example: PharmaCo Research AG submits a data access application for the diabetes cohort. MedReg DE (HDAB) reviews the request, approves it under Art. 68, and a DataPermitCredential is issued.
The Technology Compatibility Kit validat: The Technology Compatibility Kit validates that your EDC connector implements the Dataspace Protocol (DSP 2025-1) correctly. Tests cover catalog queries, contract negotiations, and transfer processes. Passing the TCK is a prerequisite for interoperability within the EHDS ecosystem.
View and manage verifiable credentials a: View and manage verifiable credentials across all dataspace participants. Each participant holds a MembershipCredential and an {credential}, issued by the trusted issuer service. Credentials follow the DCP v1.0 standard for decentralised claims, enabling trust without a central authority.
Example: The operator verifies that all: Example: The operator verifies that all 5 participants (AlphaKlinik Berlin, PharmaCo Research AG, MedReg DE, Limburg Medical Centre, Institut de Recherche Santé) each hold 2 active credentials.
A data user applies for a data permit wi: A data user applies for a data permit with the eleven items of Regulation (EU) 2025/327 Art. 67(2), then follows what becomes of it: the access body's clock (Art. 68(4)), a notice that items are missing, the permit or the refusal, and the results the user communicates afterwards (Art. 61(4)).
Example: PharmaCo Research AG applies fo: Example: PharmaCo Research AG applies for the Type 2 Diabetes Cohort and sees the access body's decision deadline count down.
A health data request under Art. 69: the: A health data request under Art. 69: the data user asks a question and, if the access body approves, receives an anonymised statistic and nothing else. The access body decides on the same page.
Example: A researcher asks how many pati: Example: A researcher asks how many patients in the cohort have HbA1c above 7 % and receives a single count.
Art. 63: the access body records a findi: Art. 63: the access body records a finding of non-compliance against a data user or holder, the party states its views within four weeks, the body takes a measure and publishes it; the body can also ask a party for information, answered on record.
Example: MedReg DE records a finding aga: Example: MedReg DE records a finding against a data user and the user responds within the four-week window.
The access body's register of applicatio: The access body's register of applications received and permits granted, refused or revoked (Art. 57). Any signed-in participant can read it.

What the access body tells the public ab: What the access body tells the public about secondary use (Art. 58(1)): the legal basis, the safeguards, people's rights and how to exercise them, who has access to which datasets and why, and the results of the projects.
Example: A patient reads which research: Example: A patient reads which research projects use data from AlphaKlinik Berlin and how to opt out.
How Germany, Austria, Belgium, France, t: How Germany, Austria, Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Spain implement secondary use: the legal role of the access body, the national law it acts under, how a person objects (Art. 71), the fees (Art. 62) and the dates, each with its official source. The laws are real, the organisations on the hub fictional.

The sovereign data exchange pipeline fol: The sovereign data exchange pipeline follows the Dataspace Protocol (DSP 2025-1): share assets, discover via federated catalog, negotiate contracts, manage tasks, and transfer data. This pipeline implements EHDS Art. 51 and 60 requirements for making health data available while preserving data holder sovereignty through policy-controlled access.
Publish datasets with HealthDCAT-AP meta: Publish datasets with HealthDCAT-AP metadata and ODRL access policies for the federated catalog. Define distribution endpoints, data quality attributes, and usage constraints. Data holders use this page to fulfil their obligation under EHDS Art. 60 to make data available for secondary use.

Initiate and track DSP contract negotiat: Initiate and track DSP contract negotiations with data holders. View negotiation state (REQUESTED, AGREED, VERIFIED, FINALIZED), ODRL policy terms, and counter-offer history. Contract negotiation ensures that data access terms are mutually agreed before any transfer occurs, as required by EHDS Art. 34.
Example: PharmaCo Research AG initiates: Example: PharmaCo Research AG initiates a contract negotiation with AlphaKlinik Berlin for the diabetes cohort. The negotiation progresses to FINALIZED with an EHDS Art. 33(c) research use policy.
Monitor the task queue for pending and a: Monitor the task queue for pending and active data transfer operations. Tasks track the full lifecycle from initiation through provisioning to completion, providing the audit trail required by EHDS for accountability.

View the complete history of data transf: View the complete history of data transfers, both initiated and received. Each entry includes timestamps, transfer size, protocol used, and a link to the audit trail. Transfer logging implements the EHDS requirement for full traceability of all health data movements across the dataspace.
Example: PharmaCo Research AG reviews it: Example: PharmaCo Research AG reviews its transfer history showing a completed 12 MB FHIR bulk export from AlphaKlinik Berlin, transferred via HTTP-PUSH with full W3C PROV audit trail.
Platform administrators manage participa: Platform administrators manage participants, access policies, and audit logs. The admin dashboard provides an overview of system health, active connections, and recent activity. Access requires the EDC_ADMIN role assigned through Keycloak. The operator role is defined by EHDS Art. 52 as responsible for ensuring the technical infrastructure supports interoperable, sovereign data exchange.
The admin dashboard shows system health: The admin dashboard shows system health at a glance: connector uptime, active participants, recent negotiations, transfer throughput, and credential status.
Example: The operator sees all 5 partici: Example: The operator sees all 5 participants are online, 3 contract negotiations are active, and 12 transfers completed in the last 24 hours with no failures.
Inspect the runtime status of Eclipse Da: Inspect the runtime status of Eclipse Dataspace Connector components: Control Plane, Data Plane, Identity Hub, Issuer Service, and the Connector Fabric Manager. View health checks, versions, and configuration details.
Example: The operator checks that the Co: Example: The operator checks that the Control Plane (port 11003), the FHIR Data Plane (port 11002) and the Identity Hub (port 11005) all report healthy on the local stack.
The evidence behind each secure processi: The evidence behind each secure processing environment's label, for the operator (EDC_ADMIN): the verdict, who verified it (the access body's Trustee), what was proven and what was not, the measurements, and the chain from the data permit to its policy hash, the Trustee's key release and the loaded workspace, with the SPE's last audit events. Each SPE on the operator dashboard links to it.

New policies start from a template for a permitted purpose of Art. 53 (scientific research, public health, official statistics, AI training and more), with the permitted purposes, the duration of use and the duties attached; the JSON can be edited directly.

This platform is a <b>reference implemen: This platform is a reference implementation of the European Health Data Space (EHDS) regulation. Its purpose is to demonstrate how sovereign health data exchange works in practice, combining the Dataspace Protocol (DSP 2025-1), FHIR R4 clinical resources, OMOP CDM analytics, and biomedical ontologies into a unified Neo4j knowledge graph.
<b>L1 Dataspace Marketplace</b>: Partici: L1 Dataspace Marketplace: Participants, DataProducts, ODRL policies, contracts, HDAB approvals
<b>L2 HealthDCAT-AP Metadata</b>: Catalo: L2 HealthDCAT-AP Metadata: Catalogues, datasets, distributions, data services
<b>L3 FHIR R4 Clinical</b>: Patients, en: L3 FHIR R4 Clinical: Patients, encounters, conditions, observations, medications
<b>L4 OMOP CDM Analytics</b>: Persons, c: L4 OMOP CDM Analytics: Persons, condition occurrences, drug exposures, measurements
<b>L5 Biomedical Ontology</b>: SNOMED CT: L5 Biomedical Ontology: SNOMED CT, ICD-10, RxNorm, LOINC concept mappings
The EHDS regulation defines distinct par: The EHDS regulation defines distinct participant roles to ensure accountability, data sovereignty, and patient rights across the health data ecosystem. This platform adapts its navigation, persona overview, and available actions to the signed-in user's EHDS role. Sign in at <c>/auth/signin</c> with any demo account: password equals username in local dev.
